To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the internationalization of the firm has been a major development of the postwar era.

the internationalization of firms is limited in degree but significant in nature, that the internationalization and standardization of markets is limited in both degree and nature and that the internationalization, denationalization and standardization processes depend on the development of powerful international institutions.
the growing internationalization of firms, markets, and management is not leading to a fundamental change of the world economy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: 1.
the interplay of national and international institutions and the impact of the latter on the former, and with the implications for the future development of the world economy.
the internationalization of firms, markets and institutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
internationalization is a process that has been taking place in the postwar world economy, but that it is not yet a dominant process and is not likely to be so in the near future.
the postwar international economy is not a distinct and coherent system, nor is it likely to become such in the near future.
the internationalization of firms, and markets has had a significant impact on the world economy, but that its impact has been limited and its consequences are not yet clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the internationalization process has been limited by the national structures of the economies in which firms operate.
the internationalization of firms, markets, and institutions is a process that is still in its early stages, and the outcome of which is far from being determined.

we have shown that the internationalization of firms is a process which is not only driven by the economic and technological forces of competition but also by the institutional structuring of national economies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the internationalization of firms is not only about the internationalization of markets.
the institutional structure of a national economy is an important determinant of its openness to foreign investment and trade.
there are no easy solutions for the problems that arise from the internationalization of firms.
